_register: THE ONE-LEVER CONTROL (batch 2 on a hard break or an unattributable read of canon-c195-in12-eager): the found configuration with building_cost = anchor x 1.95^era and nothing else changed (field diff: 43 building_cost fields; the §10.75 defines, not the eager set). Predictions in the register's terms: world GDP 0.95-1.08, the pool's GDP 1.10-1.30, pool W 0.62-0.70, pool U* >= 2x, pool H 3-4.5x (as the found: the cost step does not touch the hoard), PI 0.80-0.90, PP 0.80-0.90; the capital-abundance break rate as the found's (1 in 4). EXPECTED LOSS 5-8: the GDP terms improve, the hoard terms stay. THE ADOPT RULE (the loss-minimising iterator, 2026-09-17 evening): the incumbent is canon-c19-in12 at consensus loss 7.6 (F131; its clean seeds 5.3 / 9.5, its soft-line seed 44.4, one seed broken). After the pair (and the tie-breaker on F114 divergence): a HARD break in any run = the config is OUT (one broken run ends it). Otherwise read `criteria.mjs --arm <sessions>:<setup>`: the candidate REPLACES the incumbent only if its consensus loss is below 7.6 by at least 3 (the incumbent's own clean pair differs by 4, so a median of two moves by about 3 on seed noise alone) OR it is better on each of the three largest terms (the pool's GDP, the pool's hoard, world GDP) with no new soft breach; read the PER-SEED losses beside the consensus — a seed that crosses a soft line jumps by 10 x the line's weight, so two seeds at 3 and 40 are not better than two at 5 and 9. Every candidate is launched only on the user's go at the start of the sequence; within the sequence the batches follow each other under the 2+1 rule; at its end the next hypothesis is PROPOSED, not launched.
_alignment: THE 2+1 RULE (F114, the divergence test only since §10.83): after run 2, `node tools/testbed/ledger/alignment_check.mjs --arm <session>:canon-c195-in12` - DIVERGENT (exit 2) => the _tb.json as its own one-run schedule; what the config is JUDGED by is `node tools/testbed/ledger/criteria.mjs --arm <session[,session]>:canon-c195-in12` (the register: hard per run, the consensus of the intact runs, the loss).
